The trade-wind regime will continue for the Marianas. A brief trade-
wind trough with minimal upper-level support will bring scattered 
showers and potential isolated thunderstorms beginning after 
midnight at Guam and Rota, then on Friday at Tinian and Saipan. 
Showers look to clear out Friday night, resuming the drier trade-wind
pattern throughout the remainder of the forecast period. Although 
rainfall is expected, it will not nearly be enough to offset the past
few weeks of little to no rainfall. Therefore, early water 
conservation efforts are encouraged as the dry season approaches, 
which could potentially introduce abnormally dry (D0) conditions to 
the region within the next few weeks.

Marine/Surf...
Moderate northeasterlies will continue, becoming gentle to moderate
easterlies early next week. According to altimetry, combined seas 
are 5 to 7 feet outside our coastal waters with larger seas up to 10
feet found north of Anatahan. Seas are comprised of an elevated, 
long-period north swell that originated from Typhoon Cempaka, in 
addition to a trade swell. The north swell has arrived earlier than 
previously anticipated as surf along north-facing reefs was reported
at 5 to 7 feet with frequent, larger sets of 7 to 9 feet this 
morning. Therefore, a High Surf Advisory and a High Rip Current Risk 
Statement is in effect through 4 AM ChST Saturday. Surf may diminish
below hazardous criteria of 9 feet on Saturday. A headline was also 
included for elevated surf along east-facing reefs which is expected 
to persist at least through the weekend. In the long-term, the 
easterly swell may increase by a foot or two late next week. Those 
with marine interests should stay up to date with the forecast.

Eastern Micronesia...
The Near-Equartorial Trough (NET) has weakened and fragmented over 
the last 24-hours. The remaining fragment is located south of 
Kwajalein and Majuro, extending eastward to the Date Line. Little to
no impacts are expected with this fragment with the NET re- 
establishing itself over the next several days. A trade-wind trough 
will continue to promote scattered to locally numerous showers and 
isolated thunderstorms across portions of the RMI, including Majuro, 
through Friday. Otherwise, mostly isolated to low-end scattered 
showers are expected to prevail at all forecast sites through the 
weekend. Light to gentle winds will generally prevail at all forecast
points through at least early next week. Combined seas of 5 to 7 
feet will generally prevail at all forecast sites through Friday with
seas dropping a foot or two this weekend. Seas consist of a 
northeast, a north-northwest, and a small, southeast swell.

Most of eastern Micronesia is experiencing abnormally dry (D0) 
drought conditions. Try to start conserving water as we are 
transitioning into the dry season. 

Western Micronesia...
A band of convergence lies across Yap and Palau this afternoon and
will continue to produce scattered showers and isolated thunderstorms
across Yap through Friday afternoon and across Palau through Saturday
afternoon. The band of convergence looks to drift west over the next
couple of days as it weakens and eventually dissipates. Palau and 
Yap can then expect a fairly dry pattern through the first part of 
next week. For Chuuk, dry conditions look to prevail through the 
beginning of next week. Around Tuesday, models are hinting at a 
moderate trade-wind trough moving through the region, bringing an 
increase in chances for showers Tuesday at both Yap and Chuuk. If you
haven't already, now is the time to begin conserving water, as a much
drier period is moving in as dry season takes over the pattern.

Overall, not much change in the marine forecast. Seas look to remain
around the 7 foot threshold for both Yap and Palau. Surf will be 
elevated along the north facing reefs as the dominant north swell 
produces surf of around 8 feet. If the swell heights increase 
slightly higher, this could increase surf to hazardous levels Friday 
or Friday afternoon. This is not expected right now, but the 
possibility does exist. This will be monitored and if necessary a 
High Surf Advisory could be issued for north facing reefs of Yap and 
Palau. Winds will be mostly light to gentle trade winds for Palau 
and Chuuk, though Palau can expect occasional moderate winds. Gentle 
to moderate trade winds will prevail at Yap through the beginning of
next week.
